title: Nepal orders evacuations along Budhi Gandaki River after flash flood

title: Hurricane Isaias Leaves 396,000 Without Power in Florida Panhandle and Southern Alabama
content:
As what remained of Hurricane Isaias moved north on Sunday, nearly 396,000 customers in the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama were left without electricity. The storm’s remnants continued to bring moderate to heavy rainfall across the central Appalachians and the mid‑Atlantic region.

At least four deaths have been linked to the storm, and the National Weather Service warned that flash‑flooding could extend into the Appalachians. Heavy rain may also produce isolated flash floods, strong wind gusts, downed trees and power lines, and scattered outages across the southeastern United States, especially near the southern Appalachians.

Life‑threatening surf and rip‑current conditions were expected to persist along the Gulf and southeastern Atlantic coasts.
summary: Nearly 396,000 customers in the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama are without power as Hurricane Isaias moves north. The storm also caused at least four deaths and threatens flash flooding, strong winds, and life‑threatening surf along the Gulf and Atlantic coasts.

title: Taylor Knibb Wins Ironman World Title After Løvseth Collapses
content:
American triathlete Taylor Knibb secured her first Hawaiian Ironman world title in a dramatic finish at Kona. With a mile remaining in the race, Norwegian defending champion Solveig Løvseth held a lead of more than a minute over Knibb. Løvseth had established her advantage by taking the lead from Knibb within the final 10 kilometers of the 42.2-kilometer marathon run.

In the final kilometer, Knibb overtook Løvseth, who collapsed while leading the race. This performance marked one of the most dramatic finishes in the event's history for Knibb.

In the men's competition, France’s Vincent Luis claimed the world title during his debut at Kona.

title: ‘That’s when I begin to scream’: Mick Fanning on punching a great white shark
content:

The incident occurred during the final of a world tour event at Jeffreys Bay in South Africa, where Fanning was competing against fellow Australian Julian Wilson. The attack was broadcast live on television.

In the memoir, Fanning describes being locked onto his take-off spot in the lineup, scanning the horizon while assessing his position against the oncoming set. As he moved slightly further inside, he heard a big splash behind him. Glancing over his left shoulder, he caught a glimpse of a huge dark shape in the water, a sight that gripped him with a jolt of fear.
summary: The Australian surfing champion was famously monstered by a great white shark while competing against fellow Aussie Julian Wilson in the 2015 world tour event final at Jeffreys Bay in South Africa. The attack was broadcast live on TV.

He comfortably finished ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, who took second place.

In the championship battle, Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli finished third to extend his lead in the standings. His teammate George Russell recovered from a 19th-place grid start to finish ninth. Other notable results included McLaren’s Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri finishing fourth and fifth, respectively, while Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton placed sixth.

content:

The international collaboration focused on extracting biological clues from Jonathan, whose age makes him one of the oldest living animals. By analyzing his genetic material, the team identified a component that may explain how he has maintained health for nearly two centuries.

content:

The experiment leveraged the natural ability of spinach leaves to convert light into chemical energy, a capability that failing heart tissue lacks. By delivering the plant components to the cardiac cells, the scientists tested whether the added photosynthetic function could assist the struggling hearts.

title: Los Angeles faces worst mosquito season as heatwaves and El Niño boost West Nile cases
content:

This year’s conditions have been especially severe, driven by a series of heatwaves and an extra‑powerful El Niño. Residents describe the season as a “living hell,” noting clouds of mosquitoes swarming backyards and forcing diners on open‑air patios to scratch their ankles.

The surge in mosquito activity and associated health risks underscore the impact of the extreme weather patterns on the city’s public health.
summary: Heat and humidity have produced one of the worst mosquito years in recent history, with West Nile virus at a decade high. Los Angeles, now the most mosquito‑infested city in America, has seen swarms intensified by heatwaves and an extra‑powerful El Niño, leading locals to call the summer a “living hell.”

content:
A writer for The Verge announced a personal experiment with local artificial‑intelligence agents, describing the effort as “exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating.” The author, who cites concerns about sharing personal data with cloud services, is testing the feasibility of running powerful AI models on a personal computer rather than relying on remote platforms.

The series will track the author’s experience evaluating whether the performance of locally hosted AI justifies the cost of high‑spec hardware, such as computers with large amounts of RAM. The writer also notes that Apple’s recent marketing for its new Mac desktops emphasizes their capability to run such models, suggesting the devices may be part of the upcoming tests. The full account is available on The Verge.
summary: The writer begins using AI models locally to keep personal data off cloud services. They assess the cost and performance of running powerful models on personal computers, describing the process as both exciting and frustrating.
author: The Verge

title: LeapPad's rise and fall explored on Version History podcast
content:
Why the LeapPad couldn’t survive the iPad

The LeapPad, a smart book that played sounds, responded to taps, and helped children learn to read, was the hottest toy in the United States for multiple years. Its interactive features made it a popular choice among parents, though its high price and unexpected parenting questions added complexity to its appeal.

In a recent episode of Version History, David Pierce joined The Verge’s Andru Marino and Jennifer Pattison Tuohy to explain how the LeapPad worked, why it was so enticing to both kids and adults, and why the company that made it could never quite follow it. The episode is part of the fifth season of Version History, which is almost finished. The full story is available on The Verge.
summary: The LeapPad was a smart book that played sounds, responded to taps, and helped children learn to read, becoming a popular U.S. toy despite its high price. In a Version History episode, David Pierce, The Verge's Andru Marino, and Jennifer Pattison Tuohy discuss how the device worked, its appeal, and why its maker could not sustain it after the iPad.
author: The Verge

title: Resident Evil Requiem sells 8 million copies, 14th best‑selling Capcom game
content:
The horror genre is proving to be a major revenue driver, according to a recent piece in The Stepback newsletter.  

Resident Evil, a survival‑horror franchise that has existed for 30 years, saw its latest installment, Resident Evil Requiem, sell 8 million copies since its February launch, making it the 14th best‑selling game in Capcom’s history. At the same time, a reboot of the Resident Evil film series is being developed by Weapons director Zach Cre.  

The Stepback, a weekly newsletter that breaks down a single tech‑industry story, arrives in subscribers’ inboxes on Sundays at 8 a.m. ET. Readers can follow Andrew Webster for additional coverage of horror’s growing influence and opt in to receive the newsletter.  

The full story was published on The Verge.
summary: Resident Evil has been around for 30 years and its latest game, Resident Evil Requiem, has sold 8 million copies since its February launch. The sales make it the 14th best‑selling game ever released by Capcom.
author: The Verge

title: Apple’s Welcome Home event set for Oct. 13 in New York with smart‑home hub
content:
Apple is set to launch its “Welcome Home” event on October 13 in New York, where it is expected to unveil a series of smart‑home‑related updates. Reporters anticipate refreshes to the Apple TV and HomePod Mini, along with a brand‑new smart‑home hub.

The event may also introduce a new platform called homeOS and showcase partner devices from LG. According to Cupertino whisperer Mark Gurman, the long‑rumored touchscreen MacBook will not appear at this event and is slated for a later release this month.

The “Welcome Home” launch will officially begin at 9 AM ET in New York. The full details are available in the original Verge story.
summary: Apple will hold its “Welcome Home” launch event in New York on October 13 at 9 a.m. ET. The event is expected to feature refreshed Apple TV
author: The Verge

title: Startup Vurt aims to make vertical videos a TV genre
content:
A new startup called Vurt is positioning vertical video as its own genre, aiming to move the format from smartphones to widescreen televisions. The company argues that while major streaming services such as Disney Plus and HBO Max are experimenting with vertical content to counter the rise of video‑focused social platforms like TikTok and Instagram, most existing vertical series platforms remain focused on mobile viewing.

Vurt’s approach differs by targeting TV screens, seeking to evolve vertical micro‑dramas and series beyond the small‑screen experience that dominates current offerings. The startup’s strategy reflects an industry‑wide “arms race” for viewers’ attention as streaming services grapple with the perceived threat from social media video formats.
summary: Vurt says vertical videos should be treated as a distinct genre. Unlike other vertical micro‑drama platforms that focus on mobile, Vurt plans to deliver vertical series on widescreen televisions.
author: The Verge

title: Executives say voice AI has not yet reached a ChatGPT moment
content:
Executives say voice artificial intelligence has not yet arrived at a breakthrough comparable to ChatGPT.  

They note that voice AI frequently overlooks key elements in its context layer, which can cause the entire processing pipeline to fail.  

The shortcomings highlight why industry leaders believe the technology still has significant hurdles to overcome.
summary: Executives believe voice AI has not yet reached a ChatGPT moment. They note that voice AI often misses important points in its context layer, causing the whole pipeline to break.
author: TechCrunch

title: Efferon develops blood‑purification tech to combat pediatric sepsis
content:
Efferon says its goal is to eradicate the devastating toll of pediatric sepsis.  

The company, a Battlefield 200 startup, has created a blood‑purification technology designed to save children suffering from the condition.  

The new tech aims to address sepsis in pediatric patients by filtering blood, offering a potential treatment pathway for affected children.
summary: Efferon, a Battlefield 200 startup, has created blood‑purification technology. The tech is aimed at saving children by eradicating the toll of pediatric sepsis.
author: TechCrunch

title: Midday news bulletin for October 11, 2026 covers Europe and global stories
content: The latest news bulletin released at midday on October 11, 2026 offers a roundup of the most important stories from Europe and beyond. It presents the day’s latest, breaking news across a range of sections, including World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture and Travel.
summary: The bulletin invites readers to catch up with the most important stories from Europe and beyond on October 11, 2026. It includes coverage of world, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel news.
author: Euronews

title: Russian airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia kill 17, including three children
content:
Russian airstrikes struck the city of Zaporizhzhia on Saturday, 10 October, killing at least 17 people, including three children, Ukrainian officials said.  

Rescuers combed through the rubble for survivors as the city endured renewed strikes on residential areas. Ukrainian officials reported the casualties.
summary: Russian airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia on Saturday, 10 October killed at least 17 people, including three children, Ukrainian officials said. Rescuers searched the rubble for survivors as the city faced renewed strikes on residential areas.
author: Euronews

title: Denmark's Salling Group trials Hive Robots in stores for night restocking
content:
Denmark’s Salling Group has begun testing Hive Robots in its supermarkets. The humanoid machines are being trialled to manage demanding restocking tasks, allowing staff to focus on customer service.

The robots operate primarily during night hours, handling inventory replenishment while human employees are off‑shift. The trial aims to ease staff workload by shifting routine stocking work to the automated system.
summary: Denmark’s Salling Group is trialling Hive Robots in its stores. The robots handle demanding restocking mainly at night, freeing staff for customer service.
author: Euronews

title: Projectile hits Riyadh airport terminal, sparking fire
content:
Saudi-led coalition officials said an unidentified projectile struck the passenger terminal at Riyadh’s airport, igniting a fire. The incident occurred less than a day after a separate attack that killed 12 people and forced the airport’s closure.

The earlier attack prompted condemnation from the United Nations and the European Union, while the Houthis renewed their threats and Washington weighed its response. No further details on casualties or damage from the latest strike were provided.
summary: Fire was reported after an unidentified projectile struck the Riyadh airport passenger terminal. The strike came less than a day after an attack that killed 12 people, shut the airport and drew UN and EU condemnation.
author: Euronews

title: At least 139 migrants dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
content:
At least 139 migrants died when a boat capsized off Djibouti, the United Nations said. The UN’s International Organization for Migration (IOM) confirmed the death toll in the incident.

The IOM notes that tens of thousands of migrants travel from the Horn of Africa through Djibouti each year, seeking to cross the Bab el‑Mandeb Strait to Yemen and ultimately reach Gulf countries.
summary: At least 139 migrants were reported dead after a boat capsized off Djibouti, according to the United Nations IOM agency. The IOM says tens of thousands of migrants travel through Djibouti each year to cross the Bab el-Mandeb Strait toward Yemen and the Gulf countries.
author: Euronews

title: French student protests, Sophie Adenot returns from ISS, Israel marks Oct 7 anniversary
content:
A week of striking images captured French student protests, Israel’s three‑year October 7 anniversary commemorations, and the return of astronaut Sophie Adenot to Earth after an eight‑month stay on the International Space Station.  

Blockades and protests by French secondary school and university students persisted throughout the week, at times turning violent. Demonstrators continued to occupy campuses and streets, maintaining pressure on authorities.  

French astronaut Sophie Adenot landed back on Earth after completing an eight‑month mission aboard the International Space Station.  

In Israel, public events marked the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks, with ceremonies and gatherings observed across the country.
summary: French secondary school and university students kept blockades and protests going, occasionally becoming violent. French astronaut Sophie Adenot returned to Earth after eight months on the International Space Station, and Israel marked the three‑year anniversary of the October 7 attacks.
author: France 24

title: Trump says US may join Saudi strikes after Riyadh airport attack
content:
An assault on Riyadh’s airport prompted condemnation from the United Nations and a range of world leaders. The attack was described as a strike on the Saudi capital’s main aviation hub.

U.S. President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi Arabia in strikes against the Houthi movement in response to the airport attack.
summary: An assault on Riyadh's airport was condemned by the United Nations and world leaders. US President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.
author: France 24

title: Trump says Russia, Ukraine agree to energy ceasefire; Zelensky says it's new
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had reached an agreement on an energy cease‑fire.  

Both Kyiv and Moscow have not confirmed the reported deal. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky later responded that the announcement was “news for me,” adding that if Russia agrees to an energy cease‑fire, “we are ready and we will accept it.”  

No further details about the purported cease‑fire have been provided by either side.
summary: US President Trump posted on Truth Social that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire. Neither Kyiv nor Moscow confirmed the pact, and Zelensky said the development was new to him but Ukraine would be ready to accept it.
author: France 24

title: Deadliest Riyadh strike in over a decade prompts options for Saudi-led coalition
content:
Saturday’s missile strike on Riyadh, the deadliest attack on Saudi territory in more than a decade, marked a sharp escalation in the Yemen war. The assault came as Riyadh continues to support the internationally recognised Yemeni government against the Houthi rebels, who seized large sections of the Red Sea coastline in a rapid offensive last month.

The Saudi‑led coalition, which backs the Yemeni government, has pledged a firm response to the strike and is weighing its next steps. Analysts, including Dr Nawaf Obaid, Senior Research Fellow in the Department of War Studies at King’s College London, are examining the range of options available to the coalition.
summary: Saturday's attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, marked a sharp escalation in the Yemen war. Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis, who captured swathes of the Red Sea coastline in a lightning offensive last month, and the Saudi-led coalition has vowed a firm response, with options discussed with Dr Nawaf Obaid, Senior Research Fellow in the Department of War Studies at King's College London.
author: France 24

title: India’s “cockroach” movement leaders pledge Sunday to continue election protests
content:
Leaders of India's online “cockroach” movement pledged on Sunday to keep up their campaign against the election commissioner.

The vow came hours after the leaders were released from detention, a move authorities made as they sought to thwart a major demonstration.

The report was filed by correspondent Navodita Kumari.
summary: Leaders of India’s online “cockroach” movement pledged on Sunday to keep campaigning against the election commissioner. The pledge came hours after they were released from detention as authorities tried to thwart a major demonstration.
author: France 24

title: Five candidates seek to lead France's left for 2027 election as cyberattack hits primary
content:
Five candidates are competing to lead France’s social‑democratic left ahead of the 2027 presidential election. A cyberattack has disrupted the primary vote that was intended to select the party’s nominee.

The issue of whether the left can coalesce around a single candidate was examined in a discussion with Joseph Downing, Senior Lecturer in Politics and International Relations at Aston University.
summary: Five candidates are vying to lead France's social-democratic left in the 2027 presidential election. A cyberattack disrupted the primary vote, and the discussion features Joseph Downing, Senior Lecturer in Politics and International Relations at Aston University.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo to have surgery this week for small lung growth
content:
Pope Leo, 71, announced on Sunday that doctors had identified a small growth on his lung during a recent health check. He said he will undergo surgery this week to have the growth removed, marking the first health scare of his pontificate.

The announcement was made in an interview that included commentary from the network’s correspondent Seema Gupta.
summary: Pope Leo said doctors detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check. He will undergo surgery this week to remove it, marking the first health scare of his tenure as the 71‑year‑old pontiff.
author: France 24

title: Russia announces battalion of Ukrainian “volunteers” amid conflicting veteran accounts
content:
Russia announced the creation of a battalion composed of Ukrainian “volunteers” under its command. The statement introduced the unit as part of Moscow’s efforts to enlist Ukrainians willing to fight alongside Russian forces.

Veterans and former prisoners of war, however, have offered markedly different accounts of the battalion’s composition and purpose, underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the group’s actual makeup.
summary: Russia announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian “volunteers.” Veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.
author: DW World

title: Trump announces energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
content:
US President Donald Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine have reached an “energy ceasefire,” with both parties agreeing to halt attacks on oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure immediately.  

The ceasefire, described by Trump as an immediate stop to targeting energy sites, applies to both sides of the conflict.
summary: US President Donald Trump said both sides have agreed to stop targeting oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure. The ceasefire is to begin immediately.
author: DW World

title: IRGC warns of security breaches as US disables vessel attempting Hormuz blockade
content:
Hormuz attacks have intensified while attempts to end the war on Iran have stalled, according to recent reports. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warned that parties should not ignore the waterway’s “security and rules,” emphasizing heightened tensions in the strategic strait.

U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said the United States disabled a vessel that was attempting to run a blockade in the region. The incident underscores the growing risk of confrontations in the Hormuz corridor as diplomatic efforts remain unresolved.
summary: IRGC warned against ignoring the waterway's security and rules. CENTCOM said the US disabled a vessel trying to run the blockade.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Inter Milan fan shot in Milan reveals link between ultras and mafia
content:
A lifelong Inter Milan fan was shot in Milan, an incident that has brought to light a purported alliance between football’s ultras and the mafia, according to a True Crime Reports feature.  

The shooting, reported by the outlet, suggests that the violent act is connected to organized‑crime involvement with supporter groups, highlighting concerns over criminal influence within Italian football.
summary: A lifelong Inter Milan fan was shot in Milan. The incident exposed a shocking alliance between football's ultras and the mafia.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ethiopia and Eritrea tensions rise as Eritrean troops alleged in Tigray
content:
Ethiopia and Eritrea have intensified their public rhetoric, with new allegations that Eritrean troops have entered Ethiopia’s Tigray region. The accusations have deepened the existing rift between the two neighboring states.

Analysts warn that the heightened tension and claims of cross‑border incursions threaten the fragile peace that currently holds in the region.
summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea have intensified rhetoric amid accusations that Eritrean troops entered Tigray. The allegations are widening the rift between the two countries and endangering the region's fragile peace.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Houthi missiles breach Saudi air defences at King Khalid Airport
content: Repeated missile attacks by Yemen’s Houthi forces on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid Airport have highlighted shortcomings in the kingdom’s air‑defence capabilities. The series of strikes shows that even high‑tech defence systems can be penetrated, revealing vulnerabilities in protecting critical infrastructure.
summary: Repeated Houthi attacks have struck Saudi Arabia's King Khalid Airport. The attacks reveal limitations of even high‑tech air defences.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump repeatedly criticizes US military support for Ukraine and Zelenskyy
content: Donald Trump’s public remarks about Ukraine have consistently targeted both U.S. military aid and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.  According to the timeline, Trump has long criticised U.S. military support for Ukraine and has lambasted Zelenskyy since his first term in office.
summary: Trump has long criticized US military support for Ukraine. He has lambasted Zelenskyy since his first term.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US sanctions on ICC prompt call for protective action
content:
Calls to engage in “dialogue” with the United States over its sanctions on the International Criminal Court have been dismissed as ineffective, with observers urging concrete steps to safeguard the tribunal.

The commentary stresses that merely hoping for dialogue is meaningless and that immediate action is required to protect the court from the impact of U.S. sanctions.
summary: Dialogue with the US over its sanctions on the ICC is meaningless. Action is needed to protect the court.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 139 dead, including children, after boat capsizes near Obock, Djibouti
content:
Children were among the 139 people killed when a boat capsized off Djibouti, the United Nations said.

The vessel was traveling from Djibouti to Yemen with 305 people on board when it overturned near the port town of Obock on Thursday night.
summary: 139 people, including children, were killed when a boat capsized near the port town of Obock in Djibouti. The vessel was traveling from Djibouti to Yemen with 305 people on board and capsized on Thursday night, according to the UN.
author: BBC World

title: Fresh floods sweep homes and bridges in Nepal
content:
Fresh floods have swept away homes and bridges across Nepal, adding to the damage from recent heavy rains.  

The nation is still trying to recover from catastrophic floods that struck less than two months ago, events that left thousands dead and missing.
summary: Fresh floods have swept away homes and bridges in Nepal. The country is still trying to recover from catastrophic floods that hit less than two months ago, leaving thousands dead and missing.
author: BBC World

title: Ukraine hits Yandex data centre in third attack this week
content:
Ukraine carried out a strike on a Yandex data centre, marking the third attack on the Russian technology company this week, according to the report.  

The repeated targeting by Ukraine forced Yandex to suspend its operations following the latest incident.
summary: Ukraine struck a Yandex data centre, marking the third attack on the Russian tech giant this week. The attacks have forced Yandex to suspend its operations.
author: BBC World

title: Premier League clubs owned by Abu Dhabi deputy PM, Saudi fund and Monaco billionaire
content:
The Premier League, described as the United Kingdom’s greatest soft‑power export, is now owned largely by a group of ultra‑wealthy international investors. Current owners include the deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons, and a range of other investors and private‑equity funds.

The recent Manchester City case highlighted how difficult it is to regulate some of the world’s richest and most powerful entities. A leaked email from City’s in‑house lawyer, sent during UEFA’s action against the club, warned that the club could “spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years.” Earlier owners such as Albert Alexander Sr. and Peter Swales did not face comparable legal threats.
summary: Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco and a range of investors and private equity funds. The Manchester City case highlighted how difficult it is to regulate such owners, with a leaked City in‑house lawyer email saying the club would spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United and Spurs face reality as Manchester City rule‑breach saga distracts
content:
Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur have been forced to confront their own challenges as the ongoing saga of Manchester City’s alleged rule breaches briefly dominates football headlines, according to columnist John Brewin. The focus on City’s disciplinary issues has shifted attention away from the self‑inflicted wounds of both United and Spurs.

City’s controversies have highlighted historical contrasts, with the club’s last major trophy before the Abu Dhabi investment dating back to 1976. A recent “retouching job” to a 51‑year figure in the Stretford End was billed at £114, underscoring the scrutiny of financial calculations at both Etihad and Old Trafford.

For United, a recent league draw has produced the club’s poorest start to a campaign since Sir Alex Ferguson’s appointment 40 years ago, a milestone that will be marked next month. Fans nostalgically recall 2008, when Michael Carrick featured prominently in Ferguson’s European‑champion side, but the autumn of 2026 brings renewed doubt and speculation about the manager’s future.
summary: Manchester City’s rule breaches have dominated headlines, shifting focus from Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur’s own issues. A draw left United with their worst league start since Sir Alex Ferguson’s appointment 40 years ago.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Eliud Kipchoge wins first marathon in three years, sets Melbourne record
content:
Eliud Kipchoge, the 41‑year‑old Kenyan who is widely regarded as marathon’s greatest competitor, won his first marathon in three years at the Melbourne Marathon on Sunday. In his debut at the event, Kipchoge broke the race record by two seconds, finishing to the cheers of thousands of spectators at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

After crossing the line, Kipchoge said, “My body is still peaking,” adding, “I’m happy to run with the gen Zs.” The victory marked a return to marathon success for the athlete and set a new benchmark for the Melbourne race.
summary: Eliud Kipchoge, a 41-year-old Kenyan, won the Melbourne Marathon on Sunday, his first marathon victory in three years. He broke the race record by two seconds and said he is happy to run with the gen Zs.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester City set for hostile Anfield reception after guilty verdict
content:
Manchester City are set to play Liverpool at Anfield, with the match described as a “hostile Liverpool reception” following a guilty verdict that has yet to be sanctioned.  

Enzo Maresca’s Liverpool side have won five of five this season and sit top of the league, while City’s fixtures could become “moot” if the pending sanctions affect the outcome. The blog notes the “scale of the crisis” facing the Premier League, questioning whether a win for either side will ultimately matter.  

The game is framed as a “strange fixture” that will unfold amid the uncertainty surrounding the verdict and forthcoming penalties.
summary: Manchester City will play Liverpool at Anfield amid a hostile reception following a guilty verdict. Liverpool, led by Enzo Maresca, have won five of five matches and sit top of the league as the Premier League awaits possible sanctions.
author: Guardian Sport

title: I kissed Rodrigo and said thanks' - De Zerbi 'liked' Spurs red card
content: Roberto de Zerbi praised Tottenham midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur after the player received a red card in the club’s 1‑1 draw with Manchester United. The Spurs manager said, “I kissed Rodrigo and said thanks,” indicating he was pleased with the dismissal. De Zerbi’s comments highlighted his approval of the disciplinary outcome during the match.
summary: Roberto de Zerbi praises Rodrigo Bentancur after he was sent off in a 1-1 draw against Manchester United.
author: BBC Sport

title: Manchester City to visit Liverpool on Sunday amid uncertainty
content:
Manchester City are scheduled to travel to Liverpool for a match on Sunday, with the upcoming fixture marked by a high degree of uncertainty for the visitors.  

Phil McNulty examines the challenges facing the club, noting that questions about the team’s form and the relevance of their season linger ahead of the game.
summary: Manchester City will visit Liverpool on Sunday. Phil McNulty says a lot of uncertainty is hanging over them.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump schedules Montana and Arizona rallies for next week
content:
President Trump announced that he will hold campaign rallies in Montana and Arizona next week as part of his red‑state tour, with key races in each state occurring in less than a month.

The Arizona event is tentatively scheduled for Laughlin Bullhead International Airport in Bullhead City, a town near the Nevada border. The Montana rally has also been confirmed for the same week, though its exact location was not disclosed.
summary: President Trump will hold rallies in Montana and Arizona next week as part of his red state campaign swing, with important races in each state just under a month away. The Arizona rally is tentatively planned for Laughlin Bullhead International Airport in Bullhead City near the Nevada border.
author: The Hill

title: Tories aim to scrap Future Homes Standard as Kemi Badenoch pushes low‑carbon housebuilding cuts
content:
The recent party conference season highlighted sharply different approaches to climate action in the United Kingdom. The Conservative Party announced plans to scrap low‑carbon housebuilding, with Kemi Badenoch positioning the removal of the Future Homes Standard as a central plank of her bid to become prime minister at the Tory conference this week.

The Green Party expressed support for new nuclear reactors, while the Labour Party placed oil‑drilling decisions on hold. Analysts note that, should the Conservatives win the next general election, new homes could be built without solar panels, heat pumps and high‑grade insulation, a change that could raise household energy bills.
summary: The Conservative party plans to scrap the Future Homes Standard, allowing new homes to be built without solar panels, heat pumps and high‑grade insulation. Kemi Badenoch highlighted the policy at the Tory conference as part of her prime‑ministerial bid, while the Greens support new nuclear reactors and Labour has paused oil‑drilling decisions.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Scientists discover hidden fluid drainage system at back of eye in mice
content:
Scientists have identified a previously unknown cleanup system located at the back of the eye that drains fluid and waste. The finding was demonstrated in mice and reveals a new anatomical pathway for ocular fluid clearance.

The hidden system channels fluid and metabolic waste away from the eye, a process not described in prior research. Its existence suggests an additional mechanism by which the eye maintains internal balance.

Researchers say the discovery could open the door to new treatments for glaucoma, macular degeneration and other causes of blindness. The study was conducted using mouse models.
summary: Scientists have identified a previously unknown drainage pathway at the back of the eye that removes fluid and waste, as shown in mice. The discovery may lead to new treatments for glaucoma, macular degeneration and other blindness-causing conditions.
author: Science Daily

title: Neanderthals may have used birch tar glue as an ancient wound antibiotic
content:
Neanderthals may have applied a sticky substance made from birch bark to treat wounds thousands of years before modern antibiotics existed, according to new research. The material, long recognized as a prehistoric glue, appears to have also functioned as an ancient antibiotic.

Scientists recreated ancient birch‑tar production methods and tested the resulting samples, finding that each one inhibited the growth of bacteria that cause serious wound infections. The findings suggest that birch tar could have served as a surprisingly effective natural medicine in addition to its adhesive properties.
summary: Neanderthals may have used a sticky birch bark substance to treat wounds thousands of years before antibiotics existed. Researchers who recreated ancient birch tar production found that every sample inhibited bacteria that cause dangerous wound infections.
author: Science Daily

title: Olive oil before carbs slows digestion and regulates blood sugar in mice
content:
Scientists have found that the order in which food is eaten can affect blood‑sugar levels. In experiments, mice that received olive oil before carbohydrates showed a reduction in blood‑sugar spikes compared with other feeding sequences.  

The olive oil intake slowed digestion and triggered a combination of hormones and nerve signals that helped regulate blood sugar, an effect that persisted even in mice with type 2 diabetes. The results suggest that consuming olive oil prior to carbs may influence glucose control in this animal model.
summary: A simple change in eating order—giving olive oil before carbohydrates—could help prevent blood sugar spikes. Scientists found that in mice, including those with type 2 diabetes, olive oil before carbs slowed digestion and activated hormones and nerve signals that regulated blood sugar.
author: Science Daily

title: Vienna scientists create first self-stabilizing nuclear clock using thorium nuclei
content:
Scientists in Vienna have built the world’s first self‑stabilizing nuclear clock, a breakthrough that could eventually outpace the most precise atomic clocks.  

The new device measures time using the nuclei of thorium atoms rather than the electrons in atoms, making it far less sensitive to external disturbances.  

Researchers say the technology has the potential to replace existing atomic clocks as the leading standard for timekeeping.
summary: Scientists in Vienna have created the world’s first self-stabilizing nuclear clock. The clock uses thorium atom nuclei instead of electron transitions, making it less sensitive to external disturbances and potentially more precise than atomic clocks.
author: Science Daily

title: Polyethylene microplastics linked to fatty liver disease, study finds
content:
A study by researchers at Texas A&M has found that polyethylene microplastics, one of the world’s most common plastics, may contribute to fatty liver disease. The investigation revealed that exposure to these microplastics can promote liver fat accumulation, and the effect may be amplified when combined with an unhealthy diet.

The researchers noted that polyethylene was previously regarded as relatively harmless, but their findings suggest it could pose a hidden threat to liver health.
summary: Texas A&M researchers discovered that polyethylene microplastics can contribute to fatty liver disease. The effect may be worse when combined with an unhealthy diet, and the plastic was previously considered relatively harmless.
author: Science Daily

title: Simple walking adjustment eases knee arthritis pain, slows cartilage loss
content:
A year‑long clinical trial found that a simple adjustment to the angle of a person’s foot while walking can relieve knee arthritis pain. Researchers reported that the personalized walking technique reduced osteoarthritis pain by an amount comparable to medication, without the need for drugs or surgery.

The study also used magnetic resonance imaging to assess joint health. MRI scans showed that participants who adopted the foot‑angle modification experienced slower deterioration in a marker of knee cartilage health.

These findings suggest that altering walking mechanics may offer a non‑pharmacologic option for managing knee arthritis and protecting joint tissue.
summary: In a year-long clinical trial, researchers found that adjusting the angle of a person's foot while walking reduced knee osteoarthritis pain by an amount comparable to medication and without drugs or surgery. MRI scans showed participants who used the personalized walking technique experienced slower deterioration in a marker of knee cartilage health.
author: Science Daily

title: Northern lights light up UK skies, seen in Devon, Hampshire and Kent
content:
The northern lights illuminated skies across the United Kingdom on Friday and Saturday evening, offering a rare display of the aurora borealis.

Sky‑gazers as far south as Devon, Hampshire and Kent reported seeing the dazzling natural phenomenon, which is typically most visible near the Arctic Circle.
summary: The northern lights illuminated the skies across the UK on Friday and Saturday evening. Sky‑gazers as far south as Devon, Hampshire and Kent observed the aurora borealis.
author: Guardian Science

title: Panama declares emergency after 7.7 and 6.6 magnitude quakes, 100+ aftershocks
content:
Panama declared a state of emergency on Saturday after a series of aftershocks rattled communities across the country.

The aftershocks followed Friday’s two powerful earthquakes, one measuring 7.7 and the other 6.6 in magnitude. Officials reported more than 100 aftershocks, with the strongest reaching magnitude 5.8. Damage was reported in all ten of Panama’s provinces and in two Indigenous territories. The government’s emergency declaration follows the widespread impact of the seismic events.
summary: Panama’s government declared a state of emergency on Saturday as aftershocks rattled communities following two powerful earthquakes. title: CaPP3 study finds 100 mg aspirin reduces colorectal cancer risk in Lynch syndrome
content:
Aspirin rarely used for colorectal cancer prevention

People with Lynch syndrome face a significantly increased risk of colorectal cancer and other cancers because of a hereditary predisposition. Recent research indicates that acetylsalicylic acid may help reduce this risk.

The CAPP2 study, conducted in this high‑risk group, showed that a daily dose of 600 milligrams of aspirin significantly lowered the long‑term risk of colorectal cancer. A newer international study, CaPP3, suggests that a lower daily dose of 100 milligrams can achieve a similar preventive effect while producing fewer side effects, especially bleeding complications.

The CaPP3 findings were published in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology journal.
summary: The CaPP3 study shows that a daily dose of 100 mg aspirin may reduce colorectal cancer risk in people with Lynch syndrome, similar to the 600 mg dose used in the earlier CAPP2 study. The lower dose also appears to cause fewer side effects, especially bleeding complications, according to the study published in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology.

title: New dinosaur species from Zimbabwe shows differences from South African fossils
content:
Africa’s rich biodiversity, encompassing up to 25 % of the world’s animal and plant species, is shaped by a wide range of habitats—including harsh deserts, vast grasslands, dense forests, towering mountains, lush coastlines, and teeming seas. These varied environments contribute to the continent’s ecological complexity.  

The continent’s deep evolutionary roots also play a key role; many animal and plant groups originated in Africa during the distant past. Paleontologists have been excavating fossils and other material for nearly two centuries, uncovering evidence of the region’s long‑term biological history.  

These discoveries continue to illuminate the evolutionary processes that have produced Africa’s remarkable species diversity.
summary: A newly identified dinosaur species from Zimbabwe indicates that its dinosaurs differed from those found in South Africa. Paleontologists have been excavating such material for nearly two centuries, contributing to understanding Africa’s diverse habitats and evolutionary history.

content:

title: 200-year-old “grandmother” cottonwood tree felled for Trump border wall
content:

Land defenders began a tree‑sit in the ghost town of Lochiel, Arizona, in late July, taking turns on a platform high in the tree’s canopy. The group occupied the site for more than 70 days, maintaining a months‑long effort to save the ancient tree.  

The standoff with U.S. Border Patrol ended when the tree was toppled, clearing the site for the wall’s construction despite the prolonged protest.

title: University of Oulu study links early‑onset Alzheimer’s to multiple prior health problems
content:
A study by the University of Oulu and the University of Eastern Finland found that early‑onset Alzheimer’s disease—diagnosed before age 65—was preceded by a broader spectrum of health problems than those linked to later‑onset cases.  

Compared with matched controls, individuals who later received an Alzheimer’s diagnosis were more likely to experience depression, dizziness, headaches, traumatic brain injuries, epilepsy, cerebrovascular disorders, thyroid diseases and issues related to heavy alcohol use during the five years before diagnosis.  

The researchers also observed that tinnitus and hearing loss were already more common among these patients six to ten years prior to their Alzheimer’s diagnosis.
summary: A study by the University of Oulu and the University of Eastern Finland found that people who develop Alzheimer’s disease before age 65 accumulate a wide range of health problems, especially in the five years before diagnosis. Compared with matched controls, they were more likely to have depression, dizziness, headaches, traumatic brain injuries, epilepsy, cerebrovascular disorders, thyroid diseases, heavy alcohol‑related problems, and showed higher rates of tinnitus and hearing loss six to ten years before diagnosis.

title: Intensive breathing reduces brain blood flow and alters network communication, study finds
content:
Intensive breathing exercises can reduce blood flow to the brain by up to 45% and alter communication between brain networks, a new brain‑imaging study reports. The research, presented by the authors at the ECNP Congress in Munich, found that participants experienced sensations similar to those produced by psychedelic drugs, including altered perception, vivid mental imagery, a sense of unity and changes in self‑experience.  

The investigators emphasize that the altered state appears to be driven by changes in brain communication rather than the reduced blood flow alone.
summary: A brain‑imaging study found that intensive breathing exercises can cut blood flow to the brain by up to 45 % and change communication between brain networks. Participants reported psychedelic‑like effects such as altered perception, vivid imagery, a sense of unity and changes in self‑experience, and researchers said the network changes, not just reduced flow, appear central to the altered state.

content:
A microbiologist has released a step‑by‑step guide on how to meal prep safely. The guide highlights that preparing meals in bulk can help consumers save money, reduce time spent cooking and stay on a meal plan.

However, the microbiologist warns that bulk‑cooked meals also carry real risks if not handled properly, underscoring the need for safe food‑handling practices.
summary: Meal prepping helps save money, reduces time spent cooking, and supports a meal plan. However, bulk‑cooked meals can present real food‑safety risks.

title: Ultraviolet laser pulses selectively engineer diamond defects while preserving quantum qubits
content:
Ultraviolet laser pulses are being used to engineer diamond defects selectively, a technique that preserves quantum qubits within the crystal. The approach targets the tiny imperfections inside diamonds that can give the material new optical and electronic properties.

The research focuses on atomic‑scale defects, some of which can serve as quantum systems. By using ultraviolet laser pulses, scientists aim to create or modify these defects without disturbing the surrounding lattice.

The main challenge is learning how to control the defects without affecting the others, ensuring that the engineered quantum qubits remain intact.
summary: Ultraviolet laser pulses can be used to modify specific atomic‑scale defects in diamond. The method alters chosen defects without disturbing other defects that serve as quantum qubits.

title: Satya Nadella says all AI models are compromised, urges transparent safeguards
content:
Satya Nadella, Microsoft’s CEO, warned that all advanced AI models should be treated as potentially compromised. In a lengthy post on X, he outlined the dangers posed by highly sophisticated AI and argued that the industry can no longer accept AI as a “set of nested black boxes” whose advice and actions are simply accepted or rejected.

Nadella called for a more transparent system in which models can be contained, observed, and generate “tamper‑proof human readable evidence.” He noted that many of his recommendations—timely incident disclosure, independent audits, verifiable data, and containment—are already familiar to the industry.

The post emphasizes that containment is the most critical point for ensuring AI safety.
summary: Satya Nadella posted on X that we should assume every AI model is compromised. He called for a transparent system that contains models, provides tamper‑proof human‑readable evidence, and includes incident disclosure, independent audits and verifiable data.

title: Lancet assessment says AI misuse or nuclear war could wipe out humanity by 2100
content:
A new global risk assessment published by Lancet identifies nuclear war and the malicious use of artificial intelligence as the leading threats that could drive human extinction by the year 2100. The assessment was produced by a newly established commission that catalogued 17 catastrophic threats to human health over the next 75 years.

The commission’s report places AI misuse and nuclear conflict at the top of the list, alongside other major risks such as cuts to aid spending by wealthy nations, the climate crisis and childhood malnutrition. It also notes that a “realistic route to act” exists for each of the identified threats.
summary: A newly established commission's global risk assessment for the Lancet identifies 17 catastrophic threats to human health and says a realistic route to act on each exists. It warns that malicious use of AI or nuclear conflict could cause human extinction by 2100.

content: Yemen’s Houthi movement has issued a video that it claims depicts drone strikes against forces of the Saudi‑backed Yemeni government. The footage was released by the Houthis and is presented as evidence of attacks on the government troops. No additional details about the incidents, locations, or casualties were provided.

content:
Hurricane Simon has intensified to a Category 4 storm off Mexico’s Pacific coast, according to the latest reports.  

Businesses in the coastal city of Puerto Vallarta are boarding up windows as the hurricane threatens the west‑central portion of the Mexican shoreline.  

The storm’s strengthening heightens concerns for communities along the affected coast.

content:

content:

content: The Yemeni government’s military said its forces are advancing against the Houthi movement. content:
The World Health Organization (WHO) says that no plague case has been registered following the death of a Russian laboratory worker.

WHO officials added that the absence of a confirmed diagnosis remains a key uncertainty, but there is no indication of ongoing transmission.

content: Liverpool will meet Manchester City on Sunday in a match that has evolved into a recurring contest between the Premier League’s dominant sides. The fixture underscores the recent trend of both clubs frequently challenging each other for top honors in English football.

title: Matthew Renshaw scores 190 to help Australia overturn South Africa in Durban
content:
Matt Renshaw’s 190 in the first Test against South Africa at Durban helped Australia turn the tables on the hosts. The century was his first in Tests for nine years, and it came after a decade on the periphery of the side.

The decision to have Nic Maddinson open proved a bust, but it allowed Renshaw to bat at number five. He returned to the spotlight with an innings that saved Australia from peril, settled them into stability, and lifted them to dominance. Staunch lower‑order support, including a second‑highest ninth‑wicket partnership with Lyon, was also key. Renshaw batted through two extended sessions and was last man out just after tea.

Australia finished on 390, while South Africa were 27 for one before stumps.
summary: Matthew Renshaw scored 190, his first Test century in nine years, turning the match for Australia. Australia's lower order support helped them reach 390 and secure a win against South Africa.

title: Wallabies suffer first loss under Les Kiss at Eden Park to All Blacks
content:
Les Kiss’s first loss as Australia coach came at Eden Park, where the Wallabies were defeated by the All Blacks.  The defeat left Kiss standing forlornly in the centre of the ground, nursing a significant injury.

The Wallabies had entered the match on a six‑game unbeaten streak, fresh from a victory over world champions South Africa two weeks earlier.  In contrast, the All Blacks were experiencing a fourth straight defeat after three losses to the Springboks, and the Bledisloe Cup, after 25 years of Trans‑Tasman rivalry, finally appeared within reach.
summary: Les Kiss's Wallabies lost to the All Blacks at Eden Park, marking his first defeat as Australia coach. The Wallabies had been unbeaten for six games and had recently beaten South Africa, while the All Blacks were on their fourth consecutive defeat after losing three times to the Springboks.

title: Ollie Sleightholme's hat-trick powers Northampton to 71-48 win over Bath
content:
Northampton defeated Bath 71‑48 in a Premiership match that saw the side score 18 tries and rack up 119 points, the second‑highest total in league history.  

The high‑scoring game featured a hat‑trick from Ollie Sleightholme and two tries from Tommy Freeman, giving Northampton 11 of the 18 tries.  The match remains only behind the Saints’ 94‑33 victory over Bristol in May as the league’s biggest score.  

The win came as the defending Premiership champions, the Northampton Knicks, romped home against Bath.
summary: Northampton won 71-48 against Bath in the second-highest scoring Premiership match, with 18 tries and 119 points. Ollie Sleightholme scored a hat-trick while Tommy Freeman added two of the team's 11 tries.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ten-man Brighton continue fine form with battling win at Sunderland
content:
Brighton secured a hard‑fought victory at Sunderland, continuing their strong form despite being reduced to ten men after Pascal Struijk received a second‑half red card.

The match saw Jaouen Hadjam fire Brighton’s second goal low beyond Robin Roefs, prompting a mass exodus from the Stadium of Light. The stadium emptied quickly, and Sunderland manager Régis Le Bris was left with frown lines on his forehead.

The win cemented Brighton’s position in third place, boosting their points tally to 13.
summary: Jaouen Hadjam's second goal for Brighton, scoring low beyond Robin Roefs, sparked a mass exodus that emptied the Stadium of Light. Despite Pascal Struijk's second‑half red card, Brighton secured a win that cemented their third‑place position and raised their points tally to 13.

title: Henderson scores free‑kick as Chelsea, led by João Pedro, beat Bournemouth
content:
Jordan Henderson opened the scoring for Chelsea against Bournemouth with a curling free‑kick from about 20 yards, a strike that drew comparisons with David Beckham. The veteran midfielder then provided the assist for Morgan Rogers, who made it 2‑0.

The match also featured an all‑action midfield display from the oldest player to join Chelsea during the BlueCo era, while Cole Palmer appeared on a live stream earlier in the day to discuss his recent contract extension. Henderson’s goal marked his home debut, giving Chelsea an early lead in the game.
summary: Jordan Henderson scored a curling free‑kick and set up Morgan Rogers as Chelsea beat Bournemouth. The oldest player to join Chelsea in the BlueCo era also starred in midfield, with João Pedro part of the attacking charge.

title: Solanke scores late as 10‑man Spurs earn point at Manchester United
content:
Matheus Cunha’s cross from Luke Shaw found Bryan Mbeumo, who spun and finished to give Manchester United a lead after 72 minutes. The goal sparked delirious chants of “you’re going down with the City” from the home crowd, highlighting the precarious positions of both teams, with Tottenham Hotspur sitting at the bottom of the Premier League table.

Despite the late strike from Mbeumo, the match ended in a draw as Tottenham’s Brennan Johnson—referred to in the title as Solanke—equalized late in the game. This result allowed the ten-man Spurs to salvage a point against Manchester United, providing a crucial escape from defeat in a laboured contest.
summary: Solanke scored a late goal for Spurs, who were down to 10 men, securing a point against Manchester United. The match featured a quality moment when Matheus Cunha fed Luke Shaw to Bryan Mbeumo, who finished for United.

content:

content:

title: Hurricane Isaias Makes Landfall as Category 2, Evacuations Ordered in Florida, Georgia, Alabama
content:
Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic hurricane of the very late 2026 season, made landfall on the U.S. Gulf Coast on Friday night as a Category 2 storm with sustained winds of 105 mph. Forecasters warned of a dangerous storm surge, significant rainfall, flooding, and strong winds across the Gulf Coast this weekend.

Millions of residents in Florida, Georgia and Alabama were placed under evacuation orders as officials prepared for the storm. All three states issued states of emergency in response to the approaching hurricane.

The hurricane’s impact is expected to include severe storm surge, heavy rainfall, flooding, and high winds along the Gulf Coast.
summary: Hurricane Isaias, a category 2 storm with sustained winds of 105 mph, made landfall on the US Gulf coast Friday night. Millions of people in Florida, Georgia and Alabama were under evacuation orders, and all three states issued states of emergency.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Hurricane Isaias weakens to post‑tropical cyclone after Florida landfall
content:
Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, has caused at least four deaths and left hundreds of thousands of residents without power. The storm made landfall near Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph and brought heavy rain and fierce winds to the Gulf coast.

The National Hurricane Center announced that Isaias weakened to a post‑tropical cyclone early Saturday. It is expected to move across Alabama and into the Tennessee Valley, with maximum sustained winds decreasing to near 35 mph.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said no requests for search and rescue assistance had been received and that no fatalities had been reported yet, noting that people had heeded warnings and taken precautions. He warned that hazards remain after the storm and that the state has many assets in place to respond if needed.

Officials have warned of potential “spinoff tornadoes” associated with the storm.
summary: Hurricane Isaias, a Category 2 storm with 105 mph winds, made landfall near Destin, Florida, late Friday. The National Hurricane Center reported it weakened to a post‑tropical cyclone early Saturday, and Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said no search and rescue requests had been received.

title: Survey: most labs lack pediatric reference ranges for child cardiac troponin tests
content:
Most laboratories that test children for cardiac troponin lack pediatric reference ranges, a survey has found.  

Cardiac troponin is a protein released into the blood when heart muscle is damaged. In adults, measuring troponin provides a rapid assessment of heart injury and has transformed adult cardiology.  

For children, however, doctors often lack data on normal troponin measurements, making it difficult to interpret test results.
summary: A survey found that most laboratories testing children for cardiac troponin do not have pediatric reference ranges. Doctors lack data on normal troponin measurements for children, even though the test is widely used to assess heart injury in adults.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New Stability Rules Separate Quantum Phases Misclassified by Older Methods
content:
New stability rules have been introduced to distinguish quantum phases of matter, addressing a limitation in older methods that incorrectly grouped distinct phases together. While conventional phases like solids, liquids, and gases are easily recognized by their physical properties, quantum phases present a significantly more complex challenge for classification.

These quantum phases overturn traditional notions of what constitutes a phase, forcing physicists to rethink their fundamental definitions and categorization methods.
summary: New stability rules distinguish quantum phases that older methods grouped together. The rules show that quantum phases are harder to categorize than classical phases, leading physicists to rethink traditional definitions.

title: Nearly 300,000 at Risk from Himalayan Floods as Building in Flood Zones Grows 45%
content: A study published in Scientific Reports indicates that nearly 300,000 people in the Nepalese, Indian, and Chinese regions of the Himalayas may reside in areas at risk of flooding. The research highlights a significant increase in construction within these vulnerable zones, with the total area covered by buildings in potential flood zones rising by approximately 45% between 2016 and 2023.
summary: Nearly 300,000 people may live in areas at risk of flooding in the Nepalese, Indian and Chinese areas of the Himalayas. The study published in Scientific Reports found that the area covered by buildings within potential flood zones increased by approximately 45% between 2016 and 2023.

title: Scientists Build Lightsaber‑Like Laser Antenna That Transmits Radio Waves
content:
Scientists have demonstrated a new antenna design that resembles a lightsaber, utilizing a laser to generate a tunable plasma beam capable of transmitting radio waves. This innovative technology allows antennas to adjust their size and direction on demand, potentially revolutionizing wireless communications.

The development offers promising applications across several fields, including satellites, radar systems, and space exploration.
summary: Scientists demonstrated a lightsaber‑like antenna that uses a laser to generate a tunable plasma beam capable of transmitting radio waves. The technology could revolutionize wireless communications by enabling antennas to change size and direction on demand, with potential uses in satellites, radar, and space exploration.
author: Science Daily

title: MIT astronomers discover star slowly devouring brown dwarf for billions of years
content:
Astronomers have identified a peculiar star system roughly 300 light‑years from Earth in which a small star is slowly consuming a nearby brown dwarf. The brown dwarf—an object too massive to be a planet yet too small to sustain hydrogen fusion—lies close enough to the star that material is gradually being stripped away.

Unlike more dramatic cases where a star rapidly engulfs its companion, this system shows a gradual mass transfer. The process of the star stealing material from the brown dwarf is expected to continue for billions of years.

The discovery highlights a rare, long‑lasting interaction between a low‑mass star and a substellar object.
summary: Astronomers discovered a star system about 300 light‑years from Earth where a small star is slowly devouring a nearby brown dwarf. Unlike stars that rapidly swallow their companions, this one is gradually stealing material in a process that could continue for billions of years.
author: Science Daily

title: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory Finds More Efficient Fusion Route
content:
Scientists at Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory may have found a shortcut to fusion energy by reversing the traditional approach: heating plasma first, then increasing its density.  

Their calculations suggest that this method could enable future reactors to reach self‑sustaining fusion with far less energy input, while avoiding hidden problems that make ignition harder.
summary: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory may have found a more efficient route to fusion energy by heating plasma first and then increasing its density. Their calculations suggest future reactors could reach self‑sustaining fusion with less energy and avoid hidden problems that make ignition harder.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists discover five hidden brain patterns behind depression
content:
Scientists have identified five distinct brain activity patterns underlying the diagnosis of depression.  

In a study of 263 individuals with depression, researchers found that each of the five brain profiles displayed unique patterns of communication between brain regions. These differences were linked to varying symptom clusters, including anxiety, trauma, and substance abuse.  

The findings suggest that depression may not be a single biological condition but rather several distinct neurobiological profiles.
summary: Researchers studied 263 people with depression and identified five distinct brain profiles. Each profile shows different patterns of communication between brain regions and links to symptoms such as anxiety, trauma, and substance abuse.
author: Science Daily

title: Ledger wallet tampering suspected after crypto thefts linked to CryptoBillis hardware
content:
Ledger has warned that users of its cryptocurrency hardware wallet have experienced account drainings that appear linked to tampered devices sold by the reseller CryptoBillis. The company has asked CryptoBillis to halt all sales of Ledger wallets while an investigation proceeds.

Ledger confirmed that “one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant.” Images posted on X and Threads show a small circuit board positioned beneath the screen, which the company says can intercept anything displayed, including the seed passphrase shown during initial setup, and can transmit data via an embedded SIM card.
summary: Users of Ledger crypto wallets have reported account drains that appear tied to tampered hardware sold by CryptoBillis. Ledger has asked CryptoBillis to pause all wallet sales while it investigates a confirmed unauthorized hardware implant—a small circuit board under the screen that can intercept the seed passphrase using an embedded SIM card.

title: DistroKid removes songs after UMG lawsuit alleging AI‑slop pipeline
content:

Artists have taken to social media to complain that their work was removed without any notice. Musician McGwire, who describes himself as a “Video Game boy,” said six of his songs were taken down from streaming services and that DistroKid provided no communication before or after the removals. The situation has sparked concerns among independent musicians about the impact of the lawsuit‑driven purge.
summary: DistroKid confirmed it is taking down songs in response to a lawsuit filed by UMG that claims the service created an “AI‑slop pipeline.” Artists, including musician McGwire who lost six songs, say the removals happened without any notice from DistroKid.
